blocks.source: Canto XXXIV
blocks.translation: Canto XXXIV

blocks.source: «Vexilla regis prodeunt inferni
blocks.translation: “‘Vexilla Regis prodeunt Inferni’

blocks.source: verso di noi; però dinanzi mira»,
blocks.translation: Towards us; therefore look in front of thee,”

blocks.source: disse ’l maestro mio, «se tu ’l discerni».
blocks.translation: My Master said, “if thou discernest him.”

blocks.source: Come quando una grossa nebbia spira,
blocks.translation: As, when there breathes a heavy fog, or when

blocks.source: o quando l’emisperio nostro annotta,
blocks.translation: Our hemisphere is darkening into night,

blocks.source: par di lungi un molin che ’l vento gira,
blocks.translation: Appears far off a mill the wind is turning,

blocks.source: veder mi parve un tal dificio allotta;
blocks.translation: Methought that such a building then I saw;

blocks.source: poi per lo vento mi ristrinsi retro
blocks.translation: And, for the wind, I drew myself behind

blocks.source: al duca mio, ché non lì era altra grotta.
blocks.translation: My Guide, because there was no other shelter.

blocks.source: Già era, e con paura il metto in metro,
blocks.translation: Now was I, and with fear in verse I put it,

blocks.source: là dove l’ombre tutte eran coperte,
blocks.translation: There where the shades were wholly covered up,

blocks.source: e trasparien come festuca in vetro.
blocks.translation: And glimmered through like unto straws in glass.

blocks.source: Altre sono a giacere; altre stanno erte,
blocks.translation: Some prone are lying, others stand erect,

blocks.source: quella col capo e quella con le piante;
blocks.translation: This head first, and that one feet first;

blocks.source: altra, com’ arco, il volto a’ piè rinverte.
blocks.translation: Another, bow-like, face to feet inverts.

blocks.source: Quando noi fummo fatti tanto avante,
blocks.translation: When in advance so far we had proceeded,

blocks.source: ch’al mio maestro piacque di mostrarmi
blocks.translation: That it my Master pleased to show to me

blocks.source: la creatura ch’ebbe il bel sembiante,
blocks.translation: The creature who once had the beauteous semblance,

blocks.source: d’innanzi mi si tolse e fé restarmi,
blocks.translation: He from before me moved and made me stop,

blocks.source: «Ecco Dite», dicendo, «ed ecco il loco
blocks.translation: Saying: “Behold Dis, and behold the place

blocks.source: ove convien che di fortezza t’armi».
blocks.translation: Where thou with fortitude must arm thyself.”

blocks.source: Com’ io divenni allor gelato e fioco,
blocks.translation: How frozen I became and powerless then,

blocks.source: nol dimandar, lettor, ch’i’ non lo scrivo,
blocks.translation: Ask it not, Reader, for I write it not,

blocks.source: però ch’ogne parlar sarebbe poco.
blocks.translation: Because all language would be insufficient.

blocks.source: Io non mori’ e non rimasi vivo;
blocks.translation: I did not die, and I alive remained not;

blocks.source: pensa oggimai per te, s’hai fior d’ingegno,
blocks.translation: Think for thyself now, hast thou aught of wit,

blocks.source: qual io divenni, d’uno e d’altro privo.
blocks.translation: What I became, being of both deprived.

blocks.source: Lo ’mperador del doloroso regno
blocks.translation: The Emperor of the kingdom dolorous

blocks.source: da mezzo ’l petto uscia fuor de la ghiaccia;
blocks.translation: From his mid-breast forth issued from the ice;

blocks.source: e più con un gigante io mi convegno,
blocks.translation: And better with a giant I compare

blocks.source: che i giganti non fan con le sue braccia:
blocks.translation: Than do the giants with those arms of his;

blocks.source: vedi oggimai quant’ esser dee quel tutto
blocks.translation: Consider now how great must be that whole,

blocks.source: ch’a così fatta parte si confaccia.
blocks.translation: Which unto such a part conforms itself.

blocks.source: S’el fu sì bel com’ elli è ora brutto,
blocks.translation: Were he as fair once, as he now is foul,

blocks.source: e contra ’l suo fattore alzò le ciglia,
blocks.translation: And lifted up his brow against his Maker,

blocks.source: ben dee da lui procedere ogne lutto.
blocks.translation: Well may proceed from him all tribulation.

blocks.source: Oh quanto parve a me gran maraviglia
blocks.translation: O, what a marvel it appeared to me,

blocks.source: quand’ io vidi tre facce a la sua testa!
blocks.translation: When I beheld three faces on his head!

blocks.source: L’una dinanzi, e quella era vermiglia;
blocks.translation: The one in front, and that vermilion was;

blocks.source: l’altr’ eran due, che s’aggiugnieno a questa
blocks.translation: Two were the others, that were joined with this

blocks.source: sovresso ’l mezzo di ciascuna spalla,
blocks.translation: Above the middle part of either shoulder,

blocks.source: e sé giugnieno al loco de la cresta:
blocks.translation: And they were joined together at the crest;

blocks.source: e la destra parea tra bianca e gialla;
blocks.translation: And the right-hand one seemed ’twixt white and yellow;

blocks.source: la sinistra a vedere era tal, quali
blocks.translation: The left was such to look upon as those

blocks.source: vegnon di là onde ’l Nilo s’avvalla.
blocks.translation: Who come from where the Nile falls valley-ward.

blocks.source: Sotto ciascuna uscivan due grand’ ali,
blocks.translation: Underneath each came forth two mighty wings,

blocks.source: quanto si convenia a tanto uccello:
blocks.translation: Such as befitting were so great a bird;

blocks.source: vele di mar non vid’ io mai cotali.
blocks.translation: Sails of the sea I never saw so large.

blocks.source: Non avean penne, ma di vispistrello
blocks.translation: No feathers had they, but as of a bat

blocks.source: era lor modo; e quelle svolazzava,
blocks.translation: Their fashion was; and he was waving them,

blocks.source: sì che tre venti si movean da ello:
blocks.translation: So that three winds proceeded forth therefrom.

blocks.source: quindi Cocito tutto s’aggelava.
blocks.translation: Thereby Cocytus wholly was congealed.

blocks.source: Con sei occhi piangëa, e per tre menti
blocks.translation: With six eyes did he weep, and down three chins

blocks.source: gocciava ’l pianto e sanguinosa bava.
blocks.translation: Trickled the tear-drops and the bloody drivel.

blocks.source: Da ogne bocca dirompea co’ denti
blocks.translation: At every mouth he with his teeth was crunching

blocks.source: un peccatore, a guisa di maciulla,
blocks.translation: A sinner, in the manner of a brake,

blocks.source: sì che tre ne facea così dolenti.
blocks.translation: So that he three of them tormented thus.

blocks.source: A quel dinanzi il mordere era nulla
blocks.translation: To him in front the biting was as naught

blocks.source: verso ’l graffiar, che talvolta la schiena
blocks.translation: Unto the clawing, for sometimes the back

blocks.source: rimanea de la pelle tutta brulla.
blocks.translation: Utterly stripped of all the skin remained.

blocks.source: «Quell’ anima là sù c’ha maggior pena»,
blocks.translation: “That soul up there which has the greatest pain,”

blocks.source: disse ’l maestro, «è Giuda Scarïotto,
blocks.translation: The Master said, “is Judas Iscariot;

blocks.source: che ’l capo ha dentro e fuor le gambe mena.
blocks.translation: With head inside, he plies his legs without.

blocks.source: De li altri due c’hanno il capo di sotto,
blocks.translation: Of the two others, who head downward are,

blocks.source: quel che pende dal nero ceffo è Bruto:
blocks.translation: The one who hangs from the black jowl is Brutus;

blocks.source: vedi come si storce, e non fa motto!;
blocks.translation: See how he writhes himself, and speaks no word.

blocks.source: e l’altro è Cassio, che par sì membruto.
blocks.translation: And the other, who so stalwart seems, is Cassius.

blocks.source: Ma la notte risurge, e oramai
blocks.translation: But night is reascending, and ’tis time

blocks.source: è da partir, ché tutto avem veduto».
blocks.translation: That we depart, for we have seen the whole.”

blocks.source: Com’ a lui piacque, il collo li avvinghiai;
blocks.translation: As seemed him good, I clasped him round the neck,

blocks.source: ed el prese di tempo e loco poste,
blocks.translation: And he the vantage seized of time and place,

blocks.source: e quando l’ali fuoro aperte assai,
blocks.translation: And when the wings were opened wide apart,

blocks.source: appigliò sé a le vellute coste;
blocks.translation: He laid fast hold upon the shaggy sides;

blocks.source: di vello in vello giù discese poscia
blocks.translation: From fell to fell descended downward then

blocks.source: tra ’l folto pelo e le gelate croste.
blocks.translation: Between the thick hair and the frozen crust.

blocks.source: Quando noi fummo là dove la coscia
blocks.translation: When we were come to where the thigh revolves

blocks.source: si volge, a punto in sul grosso de l’anche,
blocks.translation: Exactly on the thickness of the haunch,

blocks.source: lo duca, con fatica e con angoscia,
blocks.translation: The Guide, with labour and with hard-drawn breath,

blocks.source: volse la testa ov’ elli avea le zanche,
blocks.translation: Turned round his head where he had had his legs,

blocks.source: e aggrappossi al pel com’ om che sale,
blocks.translation: And grappled to the hair, as one who mounts,

blocks.source: sì che ’n inferno i’ credea tornar anche.
blocks.translation: So that to Hell I thought we were returning.

blocks.source: «Attienti ben, ché per cotali scale»,
blocks.translation: “Keep fast thy hold, for by such stairs as these,”

blocks.source: disse ’l maestro, ansando com’ uom lasso,
blocks.translation: The Master said, panting as one fatigued,

blocks.source: «conviensi dipartir da tanto male».
blocks.translation: “Must we perforce depart from so much evil.”

blocks.source: Poi uscì fuor per lo fóro d’un sasso
blocks.translation: Then through the opening of a rock he issued,

blocks.source: e puose me in su l’orlo a sedere;
blocks.translation: And down upon the margin seated me;

blocks.source: appresso porse a me l’accorto passo.
blocks.translation: Then with a cautious step he joined me there.

blocks.source: Io levai li occhi e credetti vedere
blocks.translation: I lifted up mine eyes and thought to see

blocks.source: Lucifero com’ io l’avea lasciato,
blocks.translation: Lucifer in the same way I had left him;

blocks.source: e vidili le gambe in sù tenere;
blocks.translation: And I beheld him upward hold his legs.

blocks.source: e s’io divenni allora travagliato,
blocks.translation: And if I then became disquieted,

blocks.source: la gente grossa il pensi, che non vede
blocks.translation: Let stolid people think who do not see

blocks.source: qual è quel punto ch’io avea passato.
blocks.translation: What the point is beyond which I had passed.

blocks.source: «Lèvati sù», disse ’l maestro, «in piede:
blocks.translation: “Rise up,” the Master said, “upon thy feet;

blocks.source: la via è lunga e ’l cammino è malvagio,
blocks.translation: The way is long, and difficult the road,

blocks.source: e già il sole a mezza terza riede».
blocks.translation: And now the sun to middle-tierce returns.”

blocks.source: Non era camminata di palagio
blocks.translation: It was not any palace corridor

blocks.source: là ’v’ eravam, ma natural burella
blocks.translation: There where we were, but dungeon natural,

blocks.source: ch’avea mal suolo e di lume disagio.
blocks.translation: With floor uneven and unease of light.

blocks.source: «Prima ch’io de l’abisso mi divella,
blocks.translation: “Ere from the abyss I tear myself away,

blocks.source: maestro mio», diss’ io quando fui dritto,
blocks.translation: My Master,” said I when I had arisen,

blocks.source: «a trarmi d’erro un poco mi favella:
blocks.translation: “To draw me from an error speak a little;

blocks.source: ov’ è la ghiaccia? e questi com’ è fitto
blocks.translation: Where is the ice? and how is this one fixed

blocks.source: sì sottosopra? e come, in sì poc’ ora,
blocks.translation: Thus upside down? and how in such short time

blocks.source: da sera a mane ha fatto il sol tragitto?».
blocks.translation: From eve to morn has the sun made his transit?”

blocks.source: Ed elli a me: «Tu imagini ancora
blocks.translation: And he to me: “Thou still imaginest

blocks.source: d’esser di là dal centro, ov’ io mi presi
blocks.translation: Thou art beyond the centre, where I grasped

blocks.source: al pel del vermo reo che ’l mondo fóra.
blocks.translation: The hair of the fell worm, who mines the world.

blocks.source: Di là fosti cotanto quant’ io scesi;
blocks.translation: That side thou wast, so long as I descended;

blocks.source: quand’ io mi volsi, tu passasti ’l punto
blocks.translation: When round I turned me, thou didst pass the point

blocks.source: al qual si traggon d’ogne parte i pesi.
blocks.translation: To which things heavy draw from every side,

blocks.source: E se’ or sotto l’emisperio giunto
blocks.translation: And now beneath the hemisphere art come

blocks.source: ch’è contraposto a quel che la gran secca
blocks.translation: Opposite that which overhangs the vast

blocks.source: coverchia, e sotto ’l cui colmo consunto
blocks.translation: Dry-land, and ’neath whose cope was put to death

blocks.source: fu l’uom che nacque e visse sanza pecca;
blocks.translation: The Man who without sin was born and lived.

blocks.source: tu haï i piedi in su picciola spera
blocks.translation: Thou hast thy feet upon the little sphere

blocks.source: che l’altra faccia fa de la Giudecca.
blocks.translation: Which makes the other face of the Judecca.

blocks.source: Qui è da man, quando di là è sera;
blocks.translation: Here it is morn when it is evening there;

blocks.source: e questi, che ne fé scala col pelo,
blocks.translation: And he who with his hair a stairway made us

blocks.source: fitto è ancora sì come prim’ era.
blocks.translation: Still fixed remaineth as he was before.

blocks.source: Da questa parte cadde giù dal cielo;
blocks.translation: Upon this side he fell down out of heaven;

blocks.source: e la terra, che pria di qua si sporse,
blocks.translation: And all the land, that whilom here emerged,

blocks.source: per paura di lui fé del mar velo,
blocks.translation: For fear of him made of the sea a veil,

blocks.source: e venne a l’emisperio nostro; e forse
blocks.translation: And came to our hemisphere; and peradventure

blocks.source: per fuggir lui lasciò qui loco vòto
blocks.translation: To flee from him, what on this side appears

blocks.source: quella ch’appar di qua, e sù ricorse».
blocks.translation: Left the place vacant here, and back recoiled.”

blocks.source: Luogo è là giù da Belzebù remoto
blocks.translation: A place there is below, from Beelzebub

blocks.source: tanto quanto la tomba si distende,
blocks.translation: As far receding as the tomb extends,

blocks.source: che non per vista, ma per suono è noto
blocks.translation: Which not by sight is known, but by the sound

blocks.source: d’un ruscelletto che quivi discende
blocks.translation: Of a small rivulet, that there descendeth

blocks.source: per la buca d’un sasso, ch’elli ha roso,
blocks.translation: Through chasm within the stone, which it has gnawed

blocks.source: col corso ch’elli avvolge, e poco pende.
blocks.translation: With course that winds about and slightly falls.

blocks.source: Lo duca e io per quel cammino ascoso
blocks.translation: The Guide and I into that hidden road

blocks.source: intrammo a ritornar nel chiaro mondo;
blocks.translation: Now entered, to return to the bright world;

blocks.source: e sanza cura aver d’alcun riposo,
blocks.translation: And without care of having any rest

blocks.source: salimmo sù, el primo e io secondo,
blocks.translation: We mounted up, he first and I the second,

blocks.source: tanto ch’i’ vidi de le cose belle
blocks.translation: Till I beheld through a round aperture

blocks.source: che porta ’l ciel, per un pertugio tondo.
blocks.translation: Some of the beauteous things that Heaven doth bear;

blocks.source: E quindi uscimmo a riveder le stelle.
blocks.translation: Thence we came forth to rebehold the stars.
